source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.15 Line 13 - Qualified dividend exclusion; Form ND-1 line 13; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 100,000.00 + dividends 20,000.00 = 120,000.00. Federal taxable income = 120,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 104,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 104,250.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 104,250.00. Subtractions: line 13 qualified dividend exclusion, 40% x 20,000.00 = 8,000.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 8,000.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 104,250.00 - 8,000.00 = 96,250.00. Line 19 = 96,250.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (96,250.00 - 48,475.00) = 1.95% x 47,775.00 = 931.6125, to the cent 931.61; the Tax Table row 96,250 to 96,300 gives 932; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 931.61. All 20,000.00 is qualified (Form 1040 line 3a), so the form and the projection agree here.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
The dividend exclusion is applied to all dividends; the booklet allows it only on qualified dividends (Form 1040 line 3a).
